_note: Corrections from the Gemini fact-check of 2026-11-20 (FACTCHECK.md), applied by tools/build-data.mjs. 'from' = value read from a raw file we hold (source wins); 'value' = explicit value (null = no 1-atm value); 'flag' = mark as predicted/estimated; 'why' = our explanation shown in the app. Values only available from the fact-check use source key 'fc' with Gemini's citation in 'cite' and our consistency check in 'check'.

values.why: PubChem lists an older 2477 K; the corrected value 2676 K is from Zhang, Evans & Zhang (2011), J. Chem. Eng. Data 56, doi:10.1021/je1011086.
PubChem lists 2170 K; Wikipedia and the CRC Handbook (via mendeleev) agree on 2118 K.
PubChem lists an older 1413 K; Wikipedia gives 2010 K. Not measured directly: an extrapolation (fact-check §3.3).
PubChem lists 1323 K; the measured value 1259 K is given by Wikipedia and the CRC Handbook (via mendeleev).
PubChem's 14 g/cm³ is over-rounded; α-berkelium is 14.78 g/cm³ (Wikipedia; CRC via mendeleev).
PubChem's 1.93 g/cm³ is 2–3 % high for 20 °C; Arblaster (2018) gives 1.886 g/cm³ (CRC via mendeleev: 1.873).
Helium does not solidify at normal pressure (Wikipedia: Helium). PubChem's 0.95 K is a melting point at about 25 bar (fact-check).
At 1 atm carbon never melts: it sublimes (see sublimation point). PubChem's 3823 K is not a 1-atm melting point.
At 1 atm carbon sublimes (see sublimation point) instead of boiling.
At 1 atm grey arsenic sublimes. PubChem's 1090 K is a melting point under pressure (triple point).
At 1 atm arsenic sublimes at 887 K (see sublimation point); PubChem lists that temperature as a boiling point.
Astatine has never been made in bulk, so its melting point is an estimate, not a measurement.
Francium has never been made in bulk, so its melting point is an estimate, not a measurement.
PubChem says 'Ancient'. The Wikipedia infobox gives 1824 (Ørsted); the fact-check gives 1825 for the first isolation.
PubChem says 'Ancient'. The metal was first isolated in 1808 (Wikipedia infobox; fact-check: Davy).
PubChem's 1670 does not mark the element's discovery (fact-check). Wikipedia: recognised as an element in 1810; first isolated by Moissan (1886, fact-check).
PubChem's 1854 is the first crystalline silicon (fact-check). The element was first isolated in 1823 (Wikipedia infobox).
PubChem's 1827 is an unconfirmed claim (fact-check). Ruthenium was confirmed in 1844 (Wikipedia infobox).
PubChem's 'Expected to be a Gas' is outdated: relativistic calculations predict a solid (Wikipedia infobox: solid, predicted; fact-check).
